    "Use Spring Boot auto-configuration with profiles and conditions (local 'java -jar admin', 'cf push' cloud profile, and 'ltc create' receptor profile) so the matching SPI implementation is wired automatically at runtime.",
    "Use Spring Cloud Netflix Eureka client for module self-registration; module metadata is stored via the Eureka instance metadata-map and consumed by the registry to determine module state.",
    "Support module lookup by a dedicated module name attribute in registration metadata, in addition to the default spring.application.name.",

    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Core module registry abstraction (U4)",
      "activity_description": "Implement the initial module registry abstraction: ModuleDescriptor, ModuleDescriptor.Key, ModuleStatus, ModuleRegistry/Admin SPI interfaces, common exceptions, and unit tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Receptor Admin SPI implementation (U1)",
      "activity_description": "Implement getStatus, listModules, and bulk status query against the Diego Receptor API, including DTO mapping, error handling, unit tests, and stubbed integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Cloud Controller Admin SPI implementation (U2)",
      "activity_description": "Implement the same SPI operations via cf-java-client, mapping CF applications/processes to module descriptors and status/health metrics, with unit and stubbed integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Profile-aware SPI auto-configuration (U5)",
      "activity_description": "Implement Spring Boot auto-configuration that selects the correct SPI implementation per runtime (java -jar admin, cf push admin, ltc create admin) using profiles/conditions and externalized properties, with tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3

      "activity_description": "Enable modules to self-register with Eureka on install/startup and integrate Eureka-backed discovery with the Admin SPI so registered modules can be reused to build data pipelines.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Module lookup by name (U7)",
      "activity_description": "Add repository query support to fetch modules by their module name in addition to spring.application.name, including tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 2
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Module metadata storage in Eureka (U8)",
      "activity_description": "Persist module metadata in the Eureka instance metadata-map and use it to determine current module state; includes serialization, versioning of metadata keys, and tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "End-to-end integration testing and coverage",
      "activity_description": "Write and run integration tests across local, Cloud Foundry, and ltc profiles with stubbed Eureka/Receptor/Cloud Controller endpoints, fix defects, and enhance test coverage.",

- Cloud Controller (Cloud Foundry's API)
- A new module registry abstraction
- Profile-aware SPI implementation selection
- Eureka-based self-registration of modules (Spring Cloud Services - s-c-s)
- Module search by name
- Module metadata storage in Eureka

technical_and_design_decisions: Baseline on Java 17+ and Spring Framework 6 / Spring Boot 3, consistent with the stated Spring 6 requirement.

Create a dedicated multi-module build (Maven/Gradle) in a new shared repository: one module for the core SPI abstraction and one module per SPI implementation (receptor, cloud-controller, eureka), satisfying the 'permanent location' requirement.

Define the core module registry abstraction with interfaces ModuleDescriptor (including a nested Key), ModuleStatus, and a ModuleRegistry/Admin SPI exposing getStatus(ModuleDescriptor), listModules(), and a bulk status query returning Map<ModuleDescriptor.Key, ModuleStatus>.
Implement the Cloud Controller SPI using the cf-java-client library, mapping CF applications/processes to module descriptors and health metrics.
Implement the Receptor SPI as a thin REST client against the Diego Receptor API (used by the Lattice/ltc runtime), mapping actual/DesiredLRP state to ModuleStatus.

Use Spring Boot auto-configuration with profiles and conditions (local 'java -jar admin', 'cf push' cloud profile, and 'ltc create' receptor profile) so the matching SPI implementation is wired automatically at runtime.
Use Spring Cloud Netflix Eureka client for module self-registration; module metadata is stored via the Eureka instance metadata-map and consumed by the registry to determine module state.
Support module lookup by a dedicated module name attribute in registration metadata, in addition to the default spring.application.name.
Testing stack: JUnit 5, Mockito, and stub servers (e.g., WireMock) for Receptor, Cloud Controller, and Eureka; integration tests run per profile.
assumptions: A single developer performs all work; estimates express effort in workdays (8 hours), not elapsed calendar time.
Access to a Cloud Foundry environment (Receptor and Cloud Controller endpoints), a Lattice/ltc environment, and a Eureka server is available for integration testing.
The existing Spring XD codebase and Admin SPI concepts are available as a starting point; this increment extends them rather than building a new runtime.
Third-party libraries (cf-java-client, Spring Cloud Netflix Eureka client) are stable and require no changes.
The truncated API signature in U1/U2 is interpreted as a bulk module status query: Map<ModuleDescriptor.Key, ModuleStatus> getStatus().
'ltc' refers to the Lattice CLI runtime target, wired via the Receptor implementation.
No user interface work is required; deliverables are libraries plus wiring in the XD admin process.
Peer code review effort is included in each activity; formal security audits, performance certification, and production deployment are out of scope.
Existing CI infrastructure can be reused; repository setup covers scaffolding and pipeline configuration only.

activities.activity_description: Analyze user stories U1-U8, design the module registry abstraction, SPI contracts, profile-based wiring strategy, and Eureka metadata model; produce a short design note.
Create the permanent common repository for SPI implementations with a multi-module build, dependency management, and CI pipeline configuration.
Implement the initial module registry abstraction: ModuleDescriptor, ModuleDescriptor.Key, ModuleStatus, ModuleRegistry/Admin SPI interfaces, common exceptions, and unit tests.
Implement getStatus, listModules, and bulk status query against the Diego Receptor API, including DTO mapping, error handling, unit tests, and stubbed integration tests.
Implement the same SPI operations via cf-java-client, mapping CF applications/processes to module descriptors and status/health metrics, with unit and stubbed integration tests.

Implement Spring Boot auto-configuration that selects the correct SPI implementation per runtime (java -jar admin, cf push admin, ltc create admin) using profiles/conditions and externalized properties, with tests.
Enable modules to self-register with Eureka on install/startup and integrate Eureka-backed discovery with the Admin SPI so registered modules can be reused to build data pipelines.
Add repository query support to fetch modules by their module name in addition to spring.application.name, including tests.
Persist module metadata in the Eureka instance metadata-map and use it to determine current module state; includes serialization, versioning of metadata keys, and tests.
Write and run integration tests across local, Cloud Foundry, and ltc profiles with stubbed Eureka/Receptor/Cloud Controller endpoints, fix defects, and enhance test coverage.
Write README, reference documentation, Javadoc, and usage examples; package artifacts and prepare the release of the SPI repository.
